headline: BULLISH
headline_tag: Uptrend holds as price rests right on its 50-day line

action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The model's call is to scale up acquisition budget: the longer-term trend and the last three months both lean up, with high confidence (86/100 including today's news, 76 on market data alone), so this is a reasonable time to fund growth, weighted toward channels that bring active traders rather than stablecoin-only users. Because price is sitting right on its 50-day average, about $487M left Bitcoin funds in one day, and the Fed meets on 27 October, grow the budget in steps and keep part of it flexible to pause if price closes below $80,901 (the 30-day low). This is a budget posture based on trailing data, not a price call or trading advice.

reasons: Price is 13% above its 200-day average and up 26% over 90 days.
About 67% of the last 90 days closed above the long-term average.
Price sits just 0.3% above its 50-day average ($81,344), below the $86,603 30-day high.
The 200-day average still slopes down (-1%) and price is 35% below its record.
watch: The longer picture leans up, but price sits barely above its 50-day average ($81,344) and its 30-day low ($80,901), after about $487M left Bitcoin funds in one day and ahead of the 27 October Fed decision. A close below $80,901 would test the uptrend; money returning to the funds and a move back above $86,603 would ease the worry.
analysis: Bottom line: the bigger picture still points up, but this week the mood has gone quiet and price is sitting right on a line that matters. Short term, the mood leans mildly up but looks tired: the Fear & Greed reading is a middling 55, a lot of people are still betting on a rise with borrowed money, and about $487M left Bitcoin funds in a single day. A close above $86,603 (the 30-day high) would turn this clearly up, a close below $80,901 (the 30-day low) turns it down, and in between expect choppy moves, with price under 1% above that lower line today. Money flowing back into the funds would firm this up; for now steady, explain-the-news content fits better than urgent pushes.

Over the next month the picture still leans up, but more softly than the three-month record suggests: Bitcoin is about 26% higher than three months ago and about two-thirds of the last 90 days finished above the long-term average, yet the past week is down about 2%. The main date to watch is the Fed decision on 27 October, with US 10-year borrowing costs around 5.1%. There is room to climb if price gets above $86,603 (the 90-day high), while the move fades if it slips below $81,344 (the 50-day average), only a few hundred dollars under today's $81,569. A Fed pause would support growth campaigns for active traders; a rate rise or a close below that 50-day line would weaken this lean.

On the 3-6 month view the recovery is intact and got a small lift from news: Charles Schwab said all its clients can now buy Bitcoin directly (PANews), which nudges this view up a little. Price is about 13% above its 200-day average, though that average still slopes down slightly and Bitcoin is 35% below its record. The recovery stays intact while price holds above $72,431 (the 200-day average), with $66,860 (the 200-week average) as the next floor and $124,753 (the all-time high) as the far marker. The 200-day average turning upward would strengthen this; for the business it supports steady investment in onboarding mainstream newcomers rather than short bursts.

team_notes.marketing: Keep growing in steps: the longer picture leans up and no rally or drop window is open, but price is resting right on an important line, so run steady campaigns for active traders rather than urgent pushes. Lead this week's content with Schwab opening Bitcoin to all its clients and the 27 October Fed decision.
